evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Amy: 'Let's get you quoted. I'll start with a few questions to get us on the right track and then I'll create an estimate that you can depend on.' — framing present but no time box stated and no clear wait for confirmation before moving forward.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Amy: 'Do you have any specific concern what are you most worried about or any questions that you'd like me answered on this call today?' — asked AFTER extensive probing (inventory details, floor, elevator, packing needs, box count, walking distance already covered).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised two concerns: (1) price and (2) how long it would take / wanting it done in one day. Amy acknowledged price, said 'It should be pretty straightforward the inventory straightforward' but never asked follow-up questions like 'tell me more about the timeline concern' or 'what would make one day vs two days important to you.' No real two-layer exploration.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Amy never summarized or reflected back what Jasper said. No version of 'So what I'm hearing is...' or confirmation.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Amy: 'Typically an apartment the size we would send two movers, one shock. It would take anywhere from four and a half to five and a half hours... packing is the most just part of the process. So we'd have to divide this into two days.' — gave range anchored to home size and personalized to packing scope.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Amy disclosed: hourly rate ($206), packing materials ($217 budget), travel fee ($105), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, all-inclusive of taxes/insurance/gas. Full fee transparency and commitment framing present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Amy went straight from 'Question so far?' to 'Let me send you the numbers' and continued pitching without gauging acceptance.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Amy asked 'What else?' after Jasper's unpacking question, which is minimal and not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' framing.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Call ended with 'I'll email you the quote in a minute and then feel free to reach out no deposit required if you're ready to book' — a passive close with no direct ask like 'Would you like our help with your move?'
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. No date locked (customer said 'most likely week of 5th... October 8 or 9... might be as late as October 14'), no crew size confirmed, no arrival window confirmed, no notes left for crew about customer's concerns (one-day preference, timeline sensitivity).

top_strength: Amy gathered comprehensive logistics details—property type, floor, elevator access, full inventory walkthrough, packing scope, destination address, parking, and box-count expectations—creating an accurate, well-anchored estimate in two-day format with full price transparency.
coaching_note: Section 2's 'Their Agenda' must be asked *before* any probing starts, and when concerns are raised, go two layers deep instead of acknowledging and pivoting; Section 5 (Two Promises) was entirely skipped; and Section 7 needs an explicit, unambiguous close ask ('Would you like our help with your move?') and date/crew lock-in rather than passive email hand-off.
